### TAG-147: Example 12.13 Parallel Bus

**Status:** 🟡 Partial

## Software Notes

Real, precise bug — and tracing it surfaces a deeper asymmetry worth being honest about, not just patching around.

**The immediate cause: **`fanin`'s source list is `(select<> {in1<> in2<>})` — a plain place plus a *mutex group*. `writeBoundaryPorts` (which builds the real entity) correctly *expands* a mutex group into separate ports — `in1` and `in2` individually, not one combined port. But `writeOneNetworkEntity`'s port-map code treats `matched.sources` as a flat list and calls `placeName()` directly on the group entry, which builds one *combined* name (`group_in1_in2`) instead of expanding — so the port map references a port that was never actually declared.

**Fix — mirror** `writeBoundaryPorts`'s own expansion logic on the wiring side:

```
fn writeNetworkSourceMapping(
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    writer: anytype,
    place: network.Place,
    arg_index: *usize,
    entry: network.EntryInvocation,
) !void {
    if (place.group) |group| {
        if (group.kind == .mutex) {
            for (group.places) |member| {
                try writeNetworkSourceMapping(allocator, writer, member, arg_index, entry);
            }
            return;
        }
    }
    const port_id = try placeName(allocator, place);
    defer allocator.free(port_id);
    if (arg_index.* < entry.args.len) {
        try writer.print(",\n    {s} => arg_{d}", .{ port_id, arg_index.* });
    } else {
        try writer.print(",\n    {s} => null_value", .{port_id});
    }
    arg_index.* += 1;
}

fn writeNetworkDestMapping(
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    writer: anytype,
    place: network.Place,
    output_index: *usize,
    output_names: []const []const u8,
) !void {
    if (place.group) |group| {
        if (group.kind == .mutex) {
            for (group.places) |member| {
                try writeNetworkDestMapping(allocator, writer, member, output_index, output_names);
            }
            return;
        }
    }
    const port_id = try placeName(allocator, place);
    defer allocator.free(port_id);
    if (output_index.* < output_names.len) {
        const out_id = try sanitizeName(allocator, output_names[output_index.*]);
        defer allocator.free(out_id);
        try writer.print(",\n    {s} => {s}", .{ port_id, out_id });
    } else {
        try writer.print(",\n    {s} => open", .{port_id});
    }
    output_index.* += 1;
}
```

**Worth being upfront about a real gap this exposes, not fully solved by the above:** invocation *arguments* and definition *source lists* handle `{...}` differently — a brace group in an argument list (`fanin($selin1 {$outA1 $outB1})`) gets captured as **one opaque string**, never split into two separate args, while the *same* brace syntax in a definition's source list becomes a **structured group with real members**. So here, `entry.args` has 2 entries but `fanin`'s expanded port count is 3 — the fix above makes the *syntax* valid (falls back to `null_value` once it runs out of real args), but the wiring for `in2` specifically won't be semantically correct until something also splits `{$outA1 $outB1}`-shaped argument strings back into their members. I'd treat that as its own follow-up rather than fold it into this fix — worth its own issue rather than silently claiming this is fully correct.

[TAG-188](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-188/brace-groups-in-invocation-arguments)
